feed.title: Cross-Show

bullets: Labor markets are where macro stops being abstract — risk is a household-level variable rather than a portfolio-level one.
Ignoring the household-level nature of labor market risk leads to rebuilding systems from scratch a year later, as observed across teams using Bloomberg.
Systems thinking is where the conversation gets interesting because the tradeoffs around it crosscut everything covered in the discussion.
A concrete example of systems thinking involves walking through how risk management and labor markets intersect.
The failure mode of ignoring labor market dynamics is having to rebuild from scratch a year later — a costly iteration cycle.
The practical takeaway is to pick one of the covered ideas and run it for two weeks, with the rest being iteration.
